title: USGS: one magnitude unit is about ten times the amplitude and about 32 times the energy
summary: USGS says each whole-number step in magnitude is a tenfold step in seismogram amplitude and about 32 times more energy release.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey says that because the scale is logarithmic, each whole-number increase in magnitude represents a tenfold increase in measured amplitude on a seismogram, and about 32 times more energy release. It also gives an estimate relating energy to moment magnitude: log E = 5.24 + 1.44 times Mw. It says energy magnitude and moment magnitude measure different properties, so their values are not the same. The 32-times figure and the equation are both on the page.

sources.title: Earthquake Magnitude, Energy Release, and Shaking Intensity
sources.author: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
